content.comment_body: Dear Experts, We used [product_name] [article_no] in our project. We tested, downloaded the program, and shipped the panel to the customer. The device remained powered off for one year. When powered on after that period, there was no program present in the [product_name]. No memory card or battery was involved with this unit. Is it possible for the program to be lost if the device stays unpowered for one year or longer? Please advise. Regards, [user_name].

Hello, The program should remain stored on [product_name] indefinitely unless deliberately cleared. I only encountered one situation where the program was lost, and that was due to a faulty device. Regards,

According to the manuals for [product_name], the previous comment is correct, but I've seen a few devices with similar issues; it could be a manufacturing defect. This issue may not occur again, but if it does, consider replacing the [product_name]. Regards,

analysis.insight_summary: Users observed unexpected loss of program data in [product_name] [article_no] after one year without power, leading to concerns about reliability. Feedback indicates the program should persist during extended power-off periods unless intentionally erased, but rare cases of program loss may be due to factory defects, prompting doubts about long-term reliability for these devices.
analysis.user_expectations: User anticipates the [product_name] [article_no] will retain its programmed data indefinitely, even after long periods without power, and without needing a battery or memory card.
